title: Presidential Determination on Refugee Admissions for Fiscal Year 2026
summary:
The White House has set the refugee admissions limit for fiscal year 2026 at up to 7,500 people, with priority for Afrikaners from South Africa and others who face illegal or unjust discrimination. Admissions will still follow earlier orders that require the strictest identity checks and generally allow entry only when top officials decide a case is in the national interest and does not threaten security or welfare.

This decision could help people who fall into the named priority groups, especially Afrikaners who can show they face discrimination. It may also be welcomed by those who want a smaller refugee program with stronger screening. Communities and sponsors focused on these groups could see more family reunifications and targeted support efforts.

Others may be negatively affected. Refugees from different regions or backgrounds might have fewer chances to be admitted because the overall limit is low and the priority is narrow. Since admissions remain case by case under strict rules, the actual number of arrivals could end up below the ceiling. Resettlement organizations and local service providers might face funding and planning challenges with a smaller pipeline. Families already in long lines could experience more delays.

The determination applies to the 2026 fiscal year and directs the State Department to publish it. It does not override existing policies, so the key question will be how many people are ultimately admitted and which populations are able to access the program under these conditions.
